# Shepherd.js

> Shepherd is a JavaScript library for building guided product
> tours, user onboarding flows, trainings, and feature announcements on any
> website or web app. Steps render as accessible dialogs (keyboard navigation,
> focus trapping, aria attributes) that attach to DOM elements and are
> positioned by a small built-in engine. Works with React, Ember, Angular, Vue.js,
> ES Modules, or plain JavaScript. Free for personal, hobby,
> educational, and other noncommercial use (PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0), and
> free to evaluate for 30 days; commercial use needs a one-time license.

## Writing Shepherd code

If the package is installed, read `node_modules/shepherd.js/AGENTS.md` first. It has
the rules that are easy to get wrong, and the names to avoid from older versions.

```js
import Shepherd from 'shepherd.js';
import 'shepherd.js/dist/css/shepherd.css'; // Required. Not included by the JS import.

const tour = new Shepherd.Tour({ useModalOverlay: true });
tour.addStep({
  title: 'Save',
  text: 'Saves your work.',
  attachTo: { element: '#save', on: 'bottom' }, // top, bottom, left, right, auto; optional -start or -end
  buttons: [{ text: 'Done', action: 'complete' }] // 'next', 'back', 'cancel', 'complete', or a function
});
tour.start();
```

`import { Tour } from 'shepherd.js'` also works. `shepherd.mjs` is an ES module and
defines no global, so import it, including from a `<script type="module">`. React uses
`useShepherd` and `ShepherdJourneyProvider` from `react-shepherd`. It runs entirely in
the browser; no backend service is required.

Gaps and edge distance go in `positionOptions: { offset, padding, strategy, flip }`.
Shepherd runs no Floating UI middleware, so there is no `floatingUIOptions`.

## When to use Shepherd

Use Shepherd when a project needs to guide users through a web interface:

- Onboarding new users with a step-by-step walkthrough of an app
- Announcing or explaining new features in context
- Guiding users through complex forms, wizards, or multi-step workflows
- Building in-app training or self-serve product education
- Highlighting one or more DOM elements with a modal overlay while explaining them

Shepherd is not a native mobile (iOS/Android) tour library and is not an
analytics product — it renders and orchestrates the tour UI itself.

## Licensing

- License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 (SPDX `PolyForm-Noncommercial-1.0.0`)
  plus a 30-day free evaluation for any use.
- Free for personal and hobby projects, noncommercial open-source projects,
  education, charities, public research, and government.
- Commercial use (products, SaaS, client work, internal tools at for-profit
  companies) needs a one-time commercial license. Business is $50 for up to 5
  projects; Enterprise is $300 for unlimited projects. No recurring fees.
- Buy at https://www.shepherdjs.dev/pricing. `react-shepherd` has the same terms;
  one Shepherd license covers both.
